security_audit.summary: The Markdown code fence detections for Ruby backtick execution are false positives. The skill does instruct requests to a loopback Obsidian RPC service, which can expose vault metadata and should require user awareness. No prompt injection or remote exfiltration instructions were found.

Document that the RPC service must bind to localhost and should not be exposed to other network interfaces.
Provide tool-neutral RPC parameters, or instruct agents to ask before running shell commands.

content.user_title: Query Obsidian Bases from Local RPC
content.value_statement: Obsidian Bases can hold useful project and note metadata, but querying them manually is slow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused prompts for listing bases, querying views, and reading schemas through the local plugin RPC.
actual_capabilities: Lists available Obsidian Bases through the local RPC endpoint.
Queries a named base and view for structured rows.
Requests schema information for fields in a base view.
Shows jq filters for extracting names and frontmatter fields.
Describes the expected response shape with count, paths, names, and frontmatter.
limitations: Requires the Obsidian Bases Query plugin running locally.
Only works when the local RPC service is reachable at the documented port.
Does not authenticate or manage plugin installation.
Does not transform results beyond simple jq examples.

use_cases.title: Inspect note databases
use_cases.description: Product managers can list bases and check current view names before planning updates.

use_cases.title: Review project metadata
use_cases.description: Researchers can query a base view to compare statuses, dates, and note paths.

use_cases.title: Build data extraction prompts
use_cases.description: Developers can discover schemas before creating repeatable vault reporting workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List my bases
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bases skill to list available Obsidian Bases from the local RPC endpoint. Show only base names and paths.

prompt_templates.title: Query a view
prompt_templates.prompt: Query the base at [base path] and view [view name]. Summarize row names, paths, and important frontmatter fields.

prompt_templates.title: Discover schema fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the schema for [base path] and [view name]. Explain each available field and suggest fields for a report.

prompt_templates.title: Compare filtered results
prompt_templates.prompt: Query [base path] view [view name], extract [fields], and compare rows by [status or date]. Ask before reading another base.

output_examples.input: List all bases in my vault.
output_examples.output: A short list of base names, each with its vault path when available.
A concise table-style summary with note names, statuses, dates, and paths.

output_examples.input: Show fields for my reading list base.
output_examples.output: A field inventory with names, likely meanings, and suggestions for useful filters.

best_practices: Confirm the base path and view name before querying.
Review returned note paths and metadata before sharing them outside the vault.
Keep the Obsidian RPC plugin bound to localhost.
anti_patterns: Do not query broad vault views when a focused base or view is enough.
Do not expose the local RPC port beyond the local machine.
Do not paste sensitive results into external services without approval.

faq.question: What plugin does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Bases Query plugin for Obsidian through its local RPC endpoint.

faq.question: Can it install the plugin for me?
faq.answer: No. It only documents the plugin source and assumes installation is handled separately.

faq.question: Does it send data to the internet?
faq.answer: The documented queries target localhost. Results may still contain private vault data.

faq.question: What data can it return?
faq.answer: It can return base rows, note paths, names, frontmatter values, and schema fields.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompt guidance supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I confirm before running it?
faq.answer: Confirm the Obsidian app is open, the plugin is enabled, and the target base and view are correct.
